 About
 The Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP) places high school students in Department of Navy (DON) laboratories where they will take part in real Naval research for eight weeks during the summer.
 SEAP gives academically talented high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors interested in STEM the opportunity to learn about Naval research and technology while receiving first-class mentoring from top scientists and engineers. Many SEAP interns go on to careers within the DON.
 SEAP is a competitive program limited to about 300 placements across 38 laboratories in the country. Interns are selected based on academic achievement, personal statements, recommendations, and career and research interests.
 How it Works
 SEAP places academically talented high school students interested and experienced in science and/or engineering in a DON research laboratory for eight weeks during the summer.

 Important Information
 Eligibility
 High school students who have completed at least Grade 9 (see exceptions below)
 Must be currently enrolled in high school (may be taking college-level classes for college credit)
 Graduating seniors are eligible to apply
 Must be 16 years old or older by the internship start date (see exceptions below)
 Must be a U.S. citizen (see exceptions below)
 Duration & Stipend
 The SEAP internship has a duration of eight weeks (with a possible extension up to two additional weeks). Stipend levels are determined by new and returning SEAP students and will be paid bi-weekly via direct deposit.
 Stipends are as follows:
 New participants: $4,000
 Returning participants: $4,500
 Exceptions
 Applicants should check individual lab pages for eligibility as some labs make exceptions for the following:
 Grade minimum
 Age minimum
 Permanent residents and dual citizens
 SEAP Goals
 Encourage students to pursue DON science and engineering careers
 Enhance education with mentoring by laboratory scientists and engineers
 Enable students to participate in meaningful STEM research
 Expose students to DON science & technology and research & development opportunities
